```{r setup, include = FALSE}
library(MixSIARPFN)
ok <- MixSIARPFN:::networks_ready()   # the code needs the networks (see pfn_networks())
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = ok,
                      fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5, out.width = "100%")
num <- function(x, digits = 2) if (ok) format(round(x, digits), nsmall = digits) else "?"
```

This follows MixSIAR's killer whale example (Semmens et al. 2013 data, as analysed in
Stock et al. 2018): 12 killer whales, two tracers (δ¹³C and δ¹⁵N) and five salmon
prey sources, with no random, fixed or continuous effects. It is the simplest MixSIAR
model, and a good first check. Only the fitting call differs from MixSIAR's vignette:
`run_pfn()` in place of `write_JAGS_model()` and `run_model()`.

## The data

```{r load, eval = TRUE}
mix <- load_mix_data(
  filename = system.file("extdata", "killerwhale_consumer.csv", package = "MixSIARPFN"),
  iso_names = c("d13C", "d15N"), factors = NULL, fac_random = NULL,
  fac_nested = NULL, cont_effects = NULL)
source <- load_source_data(
  filename = system.file("extdata", "killerwhale_sources.csv", package = "MixSIARPFN"),
  source_factors = NULL, conc_dep = FALSE, data_type = "means", mix)
discr <- load_discr_data(
  filename = system.file("extdata", "killerwhale_discrimination.csv", package = "MixSIARPFN"),
  mix)
mix
source
```

```{r isospace, eval = TRUE, fig.height = 5}
plot_data(mix = mix, source = source, discr = discr)
```

## Fitting the model

Residual * Process error and MixSIAR's uninformative Dirichlet prior (all
`alpha.prior` equal to 1), as in MixSIAR's vignette. The network for this error
structure is downloaded the first time it is needed (about 36 MB) and cached.

```{r fit}
time <- system.time(
  fit <- run_pfn(mix, source, discr, alpha.prior = 1,
                 resid_err = TRUE, process_err = TRUE)
)
fit
```

The fit took `r num(time[["elapsed"]], 1)` seconds.

## Results

```{r output, results = "hide", fig.show = "hide"}
out <- output_pfn(fit, mix, source,
                  output_options = list(summary_save = FALSE, plot_post_save_pdf = FALSE))
```

```{r summary-table}
knitr::kable(round(summary_table(fit), 3))
```

```{r result-plots, fig.height = 4}
out$plots$global
```

```{r eps-plots, fig.height = 3, fig.width = 3.5, out.width = "48%", fig.show = "hold"}
out$plots$Epsilon.1
out$plots$Epsilon.2
```

Each is a **marginal** posterior: the network does not give joint draws, so the
marginal means need not sum to exactly 1, and sums or ratios of proportions cannot
be computed from the output.

## Comparison with MixSIAR

```{r reference}
ref <- mixsiar_reference("killerwhale")
cmp <- compare_mixsiar(fit, ref$draws, ref$summary)
```

MixSIAR `r if (ok) ref$info$mixsiar` fitted the same model with
`r if (ok) ref$info$chains` chains of `r if (ok) format(ref$info$chain_length, big.mark = ",")`
iterations (burn-in `r if (ok) format(ref$info$burn, big.mark = ",")`), which took about
`r num(ref$info$minutes, 0)` minutes (largest Gelman-Rubin diagnostic
`r num(ref$info$max_psrf, 3)`). MixSIARPFN took `r num(time[["elapsed"]], 1)` seconds.

Means, SDs, 95% intervals and the Wasserstein-1 distance (W1: how far, on average,
one posterior's mass has to move to match the other, on the proportion scale; the
residual multipliers' draws were not saved, so they have no W1):

```{r compare-table}
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  quantity = cmp$name,
  `MixSIARPFN mean` = round(cmp$pfn_mean, 3), `MixSIAR mean` = round(cmp$mixsiar_mean, 3),
  `MixSIARPFN SD` = round(cmp$pfn_sd, 3), `MixSIAR SD` = round(cmp$mixsiar_sd, 3),
  `MixSIARPFN 95% CI` = sprintf("%.2f to %.2f", cmp$pfn_q2.5, cmp$pfn_q97.5),
  `MixSIAR 95% CI` = sprintf("%.2f to %.2f", cmp$mixsiar_q2.5, cmp$mixsiar_q97.5),
  W1 = round(cmp$w1, 3), check.names = FALSE))
```

```{r compare-global, fig.height = 4.5}
plot_compare(fit, ref$draws, block = "global")
```

```{r compare-means, fig.height = 3.5}
plot_compare(fit, ref$draws, type = "means")
```

```{r numbers, include = FALSE}
diet <- cmp[!is.na(cmp$w1), ]
gaps <- abs(diet$pfn_mean - diet$mixsiar_mean)
worst <- diet[which.max(gaps), ]
```

**What this shows.** The two posteriors are close. MixSIARPFN's means differ from
MixSIAR's by `r num(mean(gaps))` on average (MixSIAR's posterior SDs are about
`r num(mean(diet$mixsiar_sd))`), and its SDs are about the same (median SD ratio
`r num(median(diet$sd_ratio))`). The largest difference is for
`r if (ok) worst$source` (`r num(worst$pfn_mean)` against `r num(worst$mixsiar_mean)`).
